clue.text: Disabled, and one is excused from voting

parts.note: I'M is the contraction of 'I am', one speaking of oneself
an MP who is paired agrees with an opponent that both will miss a vote

explanation.surface: Someone disabled has been let off going to the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: Pairing is a Westminster arrangement: two MPs from opposing sides both stay away, so their absences cancel out.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired is a common synonym for disabled, describing reduced function of a body part or faculty.

clue.text: Girl composed verse full of ecstasy

parts.note: made as in composed or created

indicators.note: full of says one word holds another within it

parts.note: a line of poetry
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A girl wrote a poem brimming with rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeleine is a female first name, so it fits the crossword's generic girl.

clue.text: About to visit a girl grown up by this time

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a lady is a grown woman
re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to call on a girl who has matured in the meantime.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means before now or by the present moment, an adverb of time.

clue.text: Puzzle of extremely reliable boat capsizing

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the two end letters

parts.note: first and last letters

indicators.note: a capsizing vessel turns upside down, which in a down clue flips the order

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine

explanation.surface: A riddle about a dependable boat overturning.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Turned up in canoe, but missing out

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the word out is removed

parts.note: a dugout is a canoe hollowed from a log

explanation.surface: Someone appeared in a canoe but missed the outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' suggests arrived; here it means dug over, as soil is turned with a spade.
explanation.definitionFit: Dug, past tense of dig, means turned up earth with a spade or fork.

clue.text: March up and down a row of shops

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to walk back and forth showily
second meaning: a British noun for a short street of shops

explanation.surface: Someone paces along a shopping street.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade is to walk to and fro for show, and in Britain a parade is also a terrace of shops.

clue.text: Break watch: one's not always working

parts.note: to part is to break or separate
a timer is a timepiece

explanation.surface: A broken watch is one that doesn't always work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a faulty watch; the definition is a person employed for only part of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-timer is an employee working fewer hours than full time, so not always on the job.

clue.text: Decay beneath said building

parts.note: a plain synonym

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: beneath means below

explanation.surface: Rot has set in below a building, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually topped with a dome.

clue.text: Large number Hun eliminated, inspiring a terror

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one piece is drawn inside
eliminated means removed, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a hundred as a large number
taken as written, to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Many of the enemy were wiped out, which struck fear into people.
explanation.walkthrough: Hun reads as a hostile soldier, but it is just the first three letters to strike out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension, a direct synonym for terror.

clue.text: Polish river, or German

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the river forming much of the border between Poland and Germany
second meaning: the German word for 'or'

explanation.surface: A question about whether a river is Polish or German.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whose river it is; in fact 'or' is the word to translate into German.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder runs through Poland, and in German the conjunction meaning 'or' is spelt exactly the same way.

clue.text: Huge fuss about king being a control freak

parts.note: a plain synonym

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed round another

parts.note: bother is fuss or trouble
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king who makes a huge fuss about everything turns out to be a control freak.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Brother is the all-seeing ruler in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names any person or authority exercising excessive surveillance and control over others, after Orwell's dictator.

clue.text: Chelsea net billowing? That's this gone

definitions.text: Chelsea net billowing? That's this gone

indicators.note: a billowing net is pushed out of shape, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: When the ball bulges Chelsea's net, the goalkeeper's record of conceding nothing is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a goal conceded ends a clean sheet, a football term for a match without conceding.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean sheet in football means a team let in no goals; a billowing net signals a goal, so it is gone.

clue.text: Not entirely straightforward to look after soap setting

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: easy means simple, straightforward
to tend is to care for

explanation.surface: Looking after a soap opera's location isn't quite simple.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap opera set in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End of London is where the BBC soap EastEnders takes place.

clue.text: Tie finally put on to twist and knot

indicators.note: twisting the combined letters round turns their order back to front
finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of tie
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Tying a knot: pull the tie's end over and twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knot or knob, as on a plant stem or in a network where lines meet.

clue.text: Shortly officially approve introducing freezing cold transport

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something inside, so pieces go in the middle
shortly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to bless a plan is to give it official sanction
a plain synonym
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An official approves bringing in transport for freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicycles are a means of transport, so plural examples stand for the general category.

clue.text: Romantic group seek a plot for development

indicators.note: something put up for development is to be rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A group of lovers are looking for a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic' suggests lovers; it refers to the literary movement of Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake Poets were Romantic-era writers who lived in England's Lake District.

clue.text: Each day, sent in to cut one of these?

indicators.note: sent in means placed inside, so pieces go within another word

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
EA is the standard abbreviation for each
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone is sent out every day to cut grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: the thing you go in each day to mow.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a field of grass grown for hay, exactly what one cuts with a mower or scythe.

clue.text: One patronising royal house perhaps as poor — agree to differ

indicators.note: to differ is to become different, so the letters change their arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A condescending royal treats the poor as people with whom one must agree to differ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patronising' here means attending as a patron; the Royal Opera House is in London's Covent Garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who patronises the Royal Opera House attends performances there, which is what an opera fan does.

clue.text: Prove wrong to get out of bed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to expose a claim as false
second meaning, whimsical: read as de- plus a bed on a ship or in a dorm

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: de- means removing, and a bunk is a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk is to show that a belief or claim is false, an everyday synonym for refute.

clue.text: Fantasy husband off to look for pity once

indicators.note: off means removed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
to hunt is to search
ruth is an archaic word for pity, surviving in ruthless

explanation.surface: A daydreaming husband leaves to seek old-fashioned compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth is a falsehood, and a fantasy is something invented and not true.

clue.text: Blend of fragrances around garden regularly advanced

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: early means advanced in time, ahead of schedule

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A mix of scents is spread round a garden in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a tea blend scented with bergamot oil, so its flavour is a perfumed one.

clue.text: Two sorts of European closely related

parts.note: first sort: a German
second sort: E, the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Two European nationalities are said to be kin.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, European, is read two ways: as a German and as its abbreviation E.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant or pertinent, closely connected to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Cut made in Christmas liturgy

indicators.note: made in says the letters are formed inside the words that follow

parts.note: the tail of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A cut is made to the words of the Christmas service.
explanation.definitionFit: A slit is a long narrow cut or opening, as in a skirt or in paper.

clue.text: Grub puts a lot of fat on Virginia

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: lard is pig fat
VA is the US state abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Eating grub piles fat on a woman called Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like slang for food; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the larva of a beetle or similar insect, its wormlike juvenile stage.

clue.text: Burst of train speed unexciting

indicators.note: a burst scatters things, so these letters are broken up and reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sudden spurt from a train turns out to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is deliberate: a burst of speed is unexciting, which is also the slow walker's word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, pedestrian means dull, plodding and lacking inspiration.

clue.text: Show indifference right through small embrace

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: running through something means passing inside it

parts.note: a plain synonym
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone is coolly unmoved throughout a little cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug is to raise the shoulders, the gesture of not caring.

clue.text: Employ Greek and old Arab outside sporting estate

indicators.note: outside says the later pieces sit on either side of the first

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
O is the abbreviation for old
a plain synonym
a Moor is a North African of Arab or Berber descent

explanation.surface: A recruiter hires a Greek and an elderly Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: A grouse moor is British upland heather kept for shooting the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse moor is land managed for shooting game birds, so it is an estate devoted to a field sport.

clue.text: Not paired off, daughters need love first of all

indicators.note: first of all says this piece comes before the others

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
D for daughter, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Daughters who haven't been matched up need affection above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd describes the one left over when the rest are put in twos, without a partner.

clue.text: Much to dish out to audience

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard by listeners, so we go by sound

parts.note: to allot is to share out

explanation.surface: There is plenty to hand out to the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase means a great deal, a common informal stand-in for much.

clue.text: A creation of Dumas on page that arouses pity

definitions.note: a clause describing the quality rather than a noun

indicators.note: in an across answer, sitting on something means coming after it, so the first-named piece is placed second

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
one of the Three Musketeers created by Alexandre Dumas

explanation.surface: A page of a Dumas novel moves the reader to compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in writing or speech that evokes sadness or sympathy in an audience.

clue.text: Bumbling constable has fruit on stalk

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or stalk them
a small fruit

explanation.surface: A clumsy policeman has fruit stuck on a stem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalk' looks like the plant stem the fruit hangs on; it is the verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogberry is the self-important, malapropism-prone police officer in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
